title: Stale credential cache causes cross-tenant request replay during token refresh storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported 500s and sporadic tenant-misattributed requests during a routine API key rotation window. Investigations show a stale in-memory credential cache entry can be re-used during a burst of token refresh events, replaying a cached org-affinity header and causing requests to be routed with the wrong tenant context.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Dedicated cluster with per-tenant API key rotation enabled and short rotation TTL (e.g., 2m).
2) Start 50 concurrent clients performing token refresh at high QPS while leader change triggers cache reload on a subset of nodes.
3) Observe intermittent 500s and some requests executed under a different tenant ID in logs (org headers mismatch).
4) Reproduce locally by simulating cache eviction during parallel refresh goroutines (unit test harness included).
incident_timeline: 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC - Oncall alerted by customer support about spike in 5xx for customer 'AcmePayments' on Dedicated region eu-west-1.
2026-03-09 22:25 UTC - Pager duty escalation, initial mitigation: rate-limit refresh storms for affected tenant and enable safer fallback routing (global safe-mode).
2026-03-10 01:40 UTC - Engineering reproduced locally; found stale-cache replay when refresh path and gateway header rewrite race.
2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Hotfix candidate deployed to a canary with additional cache-miss validation; positive signals from telemetry.
2026-03-11 16:00 UTC - Rollout to remaining Dedicated nodes in region; scheduled private customer upgrades coordinated for 2026-03-18.
root_cause: A race between credential refresh path and the in-memory tenant-affinity cache invalidation. During rotation, a node can temporarily accept a refreshed credential, but the cached mapping from API key -> tenant ID can lag and be re-used for an unrelated request arriving on another goroutine, causing tenant scoping to be wrong. The cache stores the affinity and an ephemeral validation token; validation relied on eventual background reconciliation instead of atomic refresh semantics.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations applied: (a) rate-limited token refresh bursts for affected customers, (b) enabled safe-mode routing that requires a fresh tenant lookup on boundary hits, and (c) temporary increase to cache TTLs to reduce frequent invalidations while fix is deployed.
fix_description: Implement atomic refresh handshake for API key rotation: when a refresh occurs, update the credential cache using a compare-and-swap with the refresh epoch and attach a short-lived validation nonce. All request handling checks nonce-to-token association; if absent, a synchronous authoritative lookup to the auth service is performed. Also add observability: per-key refresh epoch and mismatch counters, and a debug endpoint to replay the last 5 affinity mappings for a key.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with feature-flag guarded atomic-refresh and extra validation. 2) Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated nodes in eu-west-1 for 3 hours with synthetic refresh storm load. 3) Monitor mismatch counters and 5xxs; if stable, 50% rollout next hour. 4) Full rollout across Dedicated and Private customers over 48 hours. 5) Post-rollout, revert temporary mitigation rate-limits.
qa_plan: - Unit tests covering CAS update and nonce validation. - Integration test harness that simulates concurrent refresh and request arrival ordering. - End-to-end smoke with a staging Dedicated cluster, exercising leader change and cache reloads. - Run fuzzing of refresh vs request concurrency for 24 hours in CI elite lanes.
follow_up_tasks: Add long-term fix in auth-service to persist refresh epoch in authoritative store (ENG-560000).
Create runbook entry for token-rotation incidents and add playbook steps for safe-mode (PM-442).
Audit other caches that store tenant-affinity (edge proxies, console tracing) and add nonce validation where appropriate.
Update customer-facing KB and incident report for affected tenants.
notes: Customer communication: Support wrote to impacted customers 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC; SOC review requested due to potential cross-tenant data access (investigation shows no persisted data access occurred).
Edge-case: Private on-prem installs with disabled background reconciliation are at higher risk; coordinate on upgrade windows.
Consider moving affinity cache to sharded persistent store for stronger consistency guarantees if load testing shows memory pressure when TTLs shorten.
